subject: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Team —

Putting together the decision docket for this week's QBR item on capacity and unit economics. I want the leadership slate to have 3 clear asks + recommended decisions so the execs can sign off without drilling into spreadsheets during the meeting. Draft agenda below — please add blockers or corrections by EOD.

Agenda (short):
- Recommend: commit to 10% additional dedicated capacity (Q4) for top 3 enterprise accounts (cost and SLA impact summarized)
- Recommend: enable prefix KV caching by default for public-hosted traffic with opt-out flow for customers who need strict consistency
- Ask: approval to run aggressive batching trial (up to 250ms latency tail) on non-latency-critical routes for 6 weeks

Required inputs from owners:
- Vivek: updated GPU spend forecast with incremental cost for +10% reserved pools (attach delta) — today
- Karthik: simulation results for batch size vs token cost and tail latency percentiles — EOD tomorrow
- Lauren: draft exec slide summarizing tradeoffs (1 slide + 1 backup table) — morning of 10/13

Attachments: cost-model-v2.xlsx (cost/commit scenarios) and batching-sim-results.pdf (sim runs).

Key constraints to surface in the deck: committed vs burst capacity economics; potential customer credit exposure if we change routing policies; and a shortfall scenario if spot pools drop by 30%.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Inference Platforms
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Marissa — quick numbers attached. Summary:
- Baseline monthly GPU cost (hosted + dedicated): $4.8M
- Incremental cost to reserve +10% dedicated for top accounts (net of expected burst savings): ~$240k/month
- If we convert 20% of burst to reserved (aggressive commit), NPV over 12 months improves by ~6% but we lose flexibility for promo-driven bursts

I flagged a couple of assumptions in cost-model-v2.xlsx: preemption risk on spot pools and network egress for private deployments. If execs want a single number, recommend presenting median-case delta ($240k/mo) and a high-impact downside ($420k/mo) if spot depletion happens.

Vivek
Director, Infra Finance

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Attaching the sim summary (also in batching-sim-results.pdf). High level:
- Batching yields average token-cost reduction of 18% at median workload when moving from static single-request path to dynamic bin-packing with max batch=32
- Tail latency (99.9p) increases by ~95ms at max batch 32; at max batch 64 we see ~220ms 99.9p increase
- KV prefix cache reduces per-request compute by ~12% on sampled production traces for embeddings-heavy routes; cache hit rate sensitivity in the sim: 60%-75%

Recommendation: run two concurrent trials — (A) conservative batch profile (max batch 32, enforce 150ms soft-tail SLAs) on background routes, and (B) cache-rollout to 50% of public traffic with monitoring gates. Both experiments have rollback playbooks and perf flags.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Thanks — I've sketched the single-slide decision view. Two small edits before I make it final:
1) Can we reduce the commitment ask to +7% and present the +10% as an accelerated option? Execs prefer smaller asks with contingent upsides.
2) Add a quick customer exposure note for Acme AI — procurement asked for a pre-signed SLA exception if we put them into reserved-only routing. We should either include the exception as part of the ask or remove Acme from the committed cohort.

I'll update the slide and share a PDF by 09:30 PT tomorrow.

—Lauren
VP, Product Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Lauren — good call on the ask sizing. Let's present +7% as the primary ask and show +10% as upside.

Procurement@acme.com — looping you in so you're aware of the ask and the proposed reserved cohort. Short version: we may recommend prioritizing committed capacity for our largest enterprise accounts to stabilize latency and capacity; that can change routing defaults for a small subset of customer traffic. If Acme needs an SLA carve-out, please send the language you'd like on a 1-pager and we'll route to legal for a quick review.

Action items final:
- Marissa: incorporate +7% primary ask into deck and add contingency bullets — morning 10/13
- Vivek: provide 3-line median/high/low cost deltas for the slide — by 10:30 10/13
- Karthik: short note on rollback gates and perf flags to include in backup table — by 10:30 10/13

Marissa

From: procurement@acme.com <procurement@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra economics decision docket — QBR prep

Marissa / Lauren — thanks for the heads-up. Acme is open to being in the committed cohort if we get a short SLA carve-out for burst handling during promotional spikes. Draft language below — please confirm whether Redwood legal needs to approve or if we can accept a product-level agreement addendum.

"Acme carve-out: Redwood will guarantee reserved capacity for Acme’s core production routes. In the event of elevated promotional traffic that exceeds reserved capacity by more than 25% for more than 4 consecutive hours, Redwood will provide a burst buffer (best-effort) and credit Acme at 50% of per-token hosted price for excess usage during the incident window."
Please advise which team to coordinate with for a DocuSign.

—J. Ortega
Procurement Manager, Acme AI
